dimensions.assessment: Affects state health agencies, pediatric cancer experts, advisory committee members, and pediatric cancer patients and their families.
dimensions.evidence: membership of the State's comprehensive cancer control coalition includes at least two members who are pediatric cancer experts

dimensions.assessment: Imposes new planning and advisory mandates on state health programs and federal agencies regarding pediatric cancer care.
dimensions.evidence: establish an advisory committee, to be known as the Cancer Control Plan Pediatric Cancer Advisory Committee

dimensions.assessment: Directs the use of existing grant funds and block grants under title V of the Social Security Act toward pediatric cancer initiatives without specifying new funding authorizations.
dimensions.evidence: to meet pediatric-specific initiatives and goals within Comprehensive Cancer Control programs

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Public Health Service Act and the Social Security Act to add new state coalition requirements, a federal advisory committee, and reporting duties.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of Health and Human Services shall establish an advisory committee

dimensions.assessment: Establishes ongoing state coalition requirements and an advisory committee with a specific two-year sunset provision following its first meeting.
dimensions.evidence: The advisory committee shall sunset on the date that is 2 years after the date of the first meeting of the advisory committee.

missing_information: Specific new appropriations or funding authorizations for the advisory committee or grant programs.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates pediatric cancer expert representation in State comprehensive cancer control coalitions, establishes a federal advisory committee, and amends maternal and child health block grant uses.
